product.amstrad-anb-386sx20.summary: The entry-level ANB, with a slower processor and half the hard drive capacity of the SX40.
product.amstrad-anb-386sx20.history: In September 1991, Amstrad offered the SX20 to buyers looking for a less expensive notebook than the SX40. Computerwoche reported a German price of about 5,000 marks. In 1992, Amstrad advertised it in Spain at 229,900 pesetas plus VAT.
product.amstrad-anb-386sx20.technical.st: A 20 MB IDE hard drive held programs and data. The Spanish advertisement specifies the capacity and Amstrad support identifies the IDE interface.
product.amstrad-anb-386sx20.technical.ut: The manual described utilities for configuring the notebook, according to an owner who cited section 4.1. SPEED changed the processor speed and DISPLAY selected EGA, MDA/Hercules or CGA modes.
product.amstrad-anb-386sx20.technical.ve: The commercial configuration has been cross-checked against contemporary advertising and press. The BluMach sheet is in research.
product.amstrad-anb-386sx20.technical.li: An attributable BIOS dump, motherboard identification and boot validation in BluMach are pending.
